title: Potted Shrimps
subtitle: Brown shrimps in spiced butter
excerpt: Tiny brown shrimps stirred through nutmeg-and-mace-spiced butter and set in small ramekins. Turned out and served at room temperature with brown toast and a wedge of lemon.

recipe.sourceNotes: Potted shrimps are one of Britain's oldest preserved seafood dishes. The technique of potting — sealing food under a layer of clarified butter — was used before refrigeration to extend shelf life. Brown shrimps (Crangon crangon) from Morecambe Bay in Lancashire are the traditional choice and are considered to produce the finest potted shrimps in Britain. The shrimps are small, sweet, and intensely flavoured. The spicing is mace and nutmeg, a combination that has been associated with shellfish in British cooking since the 17th century. They are served cold, turned out of their pots.

content.text: Brown shrimps are sold ready-cooked and peeled. Do not reheat the shrimps for too long in the butter: they only need to warm through. The butter should be gently clarified by removing the white foam, which gives a cleaner flavour. Serve the potted shrimps at room temperature rather than straight from the fridge: cold butter mutes the flavour and makes them harder to eat.

items.preparation: small cooked prawns, or brown shrimps if available from a fishmonger

content.text: Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat. Skim off the white foam that rises to the surface.
Add the shrimps, nutmeg, mace, cayenne, lemon juice, and salt. Stir over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the shrimps are warmed through. Do not let the butter boil.
Divide the shrimps between 4 small ramekins, pressing them in gently. Pour the spiced butter over them to seal. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until set.
Remove from the fridge 20 minutes before serving. Run a knife around the edge, turn out onto plates, and serve with warm brown toast and a wedge of lemon.
